message.content:
Here’s a quick rundown of the most common tools and platforms you can use to book flights—whether you’re searching online, using an app, or integrating with an API.

| Category | Tool / Platform | What it’s best for |
|----------|-----------------|--------------------|
| **Flight Aggregators / Search Engines** | **Google Flights** | Fast, clean interface; shows price trends & alternative dates. |
| | **Skyscanner** | Great for multi‑city & “everywhere” searches; compares many airlines. |
| | **Kayak** | Bundles flights, hotels, car rentals; offers price alerts. |
| | **Momondo** | Strong price comparison, especially for low‑cost carriers. |
| | **Hopper** | Uses predictive analytics to tell you when to book. |
| | **TripIt** | Organizes itineraries after booking; not a search engine but handy for management. |
| **Online Travel Agencies (OTAs)** | **Expedia** | Bundles flights + hotels + car rentals; loyalty program. |
| | **Priceline** | Known for “Name Your Own Price” and Express Deals. |
| | **Orbitz** | Similar to Expedia; offers Orbitz Rewards. |
| | **Travelocity** | Good for package deals; often has exclusive OTA discounts. |
| | **CheapOair** | Focuses on discounted fares; often has promo codes. |
| | **Hotwire** | “Hot Rate” deals for last‑minute bookings. |
| **Airline Direct Websites** | **Delta, United, American, Southwest, JetBlue, Alaska, etc.** | Best for loyalty points, seat selection, and sometimes exclusive fares. |
| | **Low‑cost carriers** (e.g., Ryanair, EasyJet, AirAsia, Spirit, Frontier) | Direct booking often cheaper than OTAs. |
| **Mobile Apps** | **Google Flights App** | Same features as web, plus push alerts. |
| | **Skyscanner App** | Mobile‑friendly search & price alerts. |
| | **Hopper App** | Predictive pricing + booking. |
| | **Airline Apps** | Seat selection, boarding passes, real‑time updates. |
| **Chatbots & Voice Assistants** | **Amazon Alexa, Google Assistant, Siri** | “Book me a flight” commands via integrated services. |
| | **Chatbot on airline sites** | Quick booking via conversational UI. |
| **API & SDK Solutions** | **Amadeus for Developers** | Flight search, booking, and ancillary services. |
| | **Sabre APIs** | Comprehensive travel data, including inventory & booking. |
| | **Travelport APIs** | Global distribution system (GDS) integration. |
| | **Skyscanner API** | Search, price alerts, and flight data. |
| | **Kiwi.com API** | Multi‑segment itineraries, “virtual interlining.” |
| | **Google Flights API (unofficial)** | For developers building custom search tools. |
| | **OpenSky API** | Real‑time flight data (not booking). |
| **Specialty & Niche Tools** | **Airfarewatchdog** | Alerts for specific routes & dates. |
| | **FlightAware** | Flight status & tracking; not booking but useful for planning. |
| | **SeatGuru** | Seat maps & comfort ratings. |
| | **Trip.com** | Strong presence in Asia; good for international flights. |
| | **Ctrip / Trip.com** | Chinese OTA with global coverage. |
| | **Booking.com Flights** | Adds flight search to hotel booking platform. |

### How to Choose

1. **Price vs. Convenience** – Aggregators give you a broad view of prices; airline sites often have the best loyalty perks.
2. **Route Complexity** – For multi‑city or “open‑jaw” itineraries, Skyscanner, Kayak, or Amadeus APIs excel.
3. **Last‑Minute Deals** – Hopper, Hotwire, and low‑cost carriers are great for spontaneous trips.
4. **Loyalty Programs** – Book directly with airlines to earn miles or points.
5. **Developer Needs** – Use Amadeus, Sabre, or Skyscanner APIs if you’re building a travel app or bot.

Feel free to let me know if you’d like deeper details on any particular platform or how to integrate a specific API!
